title: AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents
data_curation: Training data are RL environments built by a proposer agent as complete Harbor tasks (instruction, container, hidden reference solution, tests). Each episode starts from an assignment naming a parent environment plus the solver's pass rate and most common failure; the proposer reads past solver trajectories and verifier outputs and builds an easier or harder variant, with web search allowed but benchmark pages blocked. Admission requires a successful build, reference reward 1, do-nothing reward < 0.5, no 13-gram overlap with Terminal-Bench 2.1/4.0 task text, and a harbor-check review against the Terminal-Bench rubric. Calibration then keeps tasks whose mean solver reward over 4-8 rollouts lies in [0.25, 0.75] with std >= 0.1, allowing up to two revisions. For HiL-Bench, Claude Opus 5 generated 500 underspecified tasks with withheld-detail registries (vs 100 official).
curriculum: The curriculum is an online data flywheel. The solver trains on an active pool (256 tasks in the shared-model run); every 16 solver updates the pool is re-checked against the updated solver, out-of-band tasks are dropped, and the proposer builds replacements from the newest rollouts. With frontier proposers (GPT-5.6-sol, Claude Opus 5), weights are fixed and the proposer improves only its harness (memory, skills, tools) across rounds. In the self-improvement setting, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is first cold-started by SFT on 600 high-quality proposer trajectories (valid rate 32.3% -> 86.8%), then RL-trained as both proposer and solver. HiL-Bench training uses SFT on 75 ask-for-help trajectories before RL for up to 150 steps.
method: AutoEnvScaling treats environment design as a terminal task: the proposer runs in a sandbox (16 CPUs, 32 GiB, 2-hour budget) under Claude Code, Codex or Pi, launches child containers to build and test tasks, and can call the current solver to estimate difficulty. Solver reward is the fraction of tests passed. Proposer reward is -1 if validation fails, -0.25 if validation passes but calibration fails, and +1 if both pass. For open weights, one policy plays both roles under DPPO (TV threshold 0.1, LR 1e-6, no KL/entropy) with separate mean-centered advantage baselines: solver groups of 16 attempts per environment (16 envs x 16), proposer groups of 128 trajectories per assignment. Zero-variance groups are dropped DAPO-style and unfinished trajectories carry over between updates (Miles, 4-8 B200). Frontier-proposer runs use group size 16, 16 prompts per batch and 128k max sequence length.
eval_metrics: Environment generation: valid-environment rate and USD cost per valid environment for eight proposers under Prompt, Prompt+Env Feedback and AutoEnvScaling (DeepSeek-V4-Flash 3.5% -> 12.1% -> 89.0%; Claude Opus 5 74.6% -> 94.0%). Solver: held-out Terminal-Bench 2.1 avg@5 with the Pi agent (4 CPUs, 8 GiB). Qwen3.5-9B: 19.1 base, 27.2 Tmax, 33.5 AutoEnvScaling (GPT-5.6-sol). Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 26.7 base, 34.6 Tmax, 38.9 AutoEnvScaling, 35.3 without solver feedback. Self-improvement: Terminal-Bench 2.1 41.1 -> 53.3 and Terminal-Bench 4.0 1.6 -> 3.2. HiL-Bench SWE (ask_human): task success 33.9% and Ask-F1 55.3% vs 6.8%/29.6% when trained on the official tasks. Cross-domain admission: 1,061 of 1,489 runs (71.3%).
key_results: Running generation as a terminal task raises the valid-environment rate by up to 25x over prompt-only generation at up to 75% lower cost per valid environment, and RL on GPT-5.6-sol environments lifts Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 4.3 points above a matched Tmax pool on Terminal-Bench 2.1. With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as both proposer and solver, Terminal-Bench 2.1 rises 12.2 points (6.1 above Tmax); without proposer training, valid rate falls to 22.4% and training collapses.
evolution_note: AutoEnvScaling builds on terminal-environment synthesis pipelines (Endless Terminals, TermiGen, Tmax, SETA, RST) and on proposer-solver self-play (Absolute Zero, R-Zero, SPICE, SPADE). Those approaches fix the generation procedure in advance; here an agent carries out the researcher's environment-design workflow end to end, using solver rollouts and a persistent harness. Training one model in both roles, kept stable by an explicit proposer reward, is presented as a step toward recursive self-improvement through self-built training data.
